meta.source: CLAUDE.md turn 14 F5 (BACKLOG #45). There is NO AutoLISP for this part — the Skylon kits do not cut it — so the source of truth is the owner's own specification, quoted verbatim in `rules` below and traced into numbers case by case.
meta.computed_by: Claude (turn 14 autonomous session, 09.08.2026), from the specification and from the profile numbers it names — NOT from the engine.
meta.rule: GOLDEN FIXTURES - DO NOT MODIFY. Tests must make these pass. If engine output differs, the ENGINE is wrong (or file a BLOCKERS.md entry). Never edit expected values to make tests green.

mask_rules.spec: One continuous panel under a RUN of wall units: length = the sum of the run's units; depth = unit depth + 10 mm (it hides the 10 mm wall standoff). Docking a unit extends it; an end panel or gap is a boundary (reuse the run logic).
mask_rules.length: the sum of the segment's CARCASS widths, measured left carcass edge to right carcass edge — the plinth's rule (turn 12 F8), and for the plinth's reason: an end panel is the visible end of the run and the board meets its inner face rather than running behind it
mask_rules.depth: the DEEPEST cabinet of the segment + profile.room.wallBackClearance (10). One board closes the segment, and a board that is short at the back leaves the slot the piece exists to hide
mask_rules.thickness: profile.autoParts.mask.thickness ?? the project's FRONT thickness (25 by default) — F5.2 puts it through the front pipeline
mask_rules.material: FRONT. The owner's assumption per F5.2, flagged in BUILD-LOG: it stands in the room under the doors, in the plane the eye reads as the front of the run, so it is finished with them. One line in engine/cabinet.js FRONT_MATERIAL_ROLES to change.
mask_rules.position: y = -thickness (directly under the carcass floor); z = -10 (it starts at the wall, behind the carcass back) and runs forward to the carcass face
mask_rules.edging: all four coded, LENGTH = 2 x depth + 1 x length: the two ends and the FRONT edge are seen — from the room, from below, and from the side at the end of a run. The back edge is against the wall.
mask_rules.boundaries: no mask = no mask; adjacent masked wall units with no end panel between them = ONE board; an end panel or a gap starts a new segment
mask_rules.who: wall-mounted kits only — a base unit has a worktop on it and a plinth under it, and neither is this piece

cases.description: One wall unit, 600 x 720 x 300, front board 25, wall standoff 10
A RUN of three 600 mm wall units butted together: ONE board of 1800, not three of 600
A fourth unit docked onto the run extends the SAME board rather than adding one
An END PANEL between two masked units is a boundary: two boards, and each meets the panel's inner face
A GAP is a boundary too — the run itself breaks, so the board does
A base unit is refused: it has a worktop on it and a plinth under it

verify_with_piotr: FRONT material and therefore SPRAYED with the doors — F5.2 says the owner assumed it and may adjust
depth = the DEEPEST cabinet of the segment + 10, for a run whose cabinets are not all one depth
the board meets an end panel's INNER face (the plinth's rule) rather than running behind it
thickness = the front board (25). A workshop cutting it from 12 mm sets autoParts.mask.thickness
the back edge is left unbanded — it is against the wall
